38:def reindex_variables(
39:    variables: Mapping[Any, Variable],
40:    dim_pos_indexers: Mapping[Any, Any],
41:    copy: bool = True,
42:    fill_value: Any = dtypes.NA,
43:    sparse: bool = False,
44:) -> dict[Hashable, Variable]:
45:    """Conform a dictionary of variables onto a new set of variables reindexed
46:    with dimension positional indexers and possibly filled with missing values.
47:
48:    Not public API.
49:
50:    """
51:    new_variables = {}
52:    dim_sizes = calculate_dimensions(variables)
53:
54:    masked_dims = set()
55:    unchanged_dims = set()
56:    for dim, indxr in dim_pos_indexers.items():
57:        # Negative values in dim_pos_indexers mean values missing in the new index
58:        # See ``Index.reindex_like``.
59:        if (indxr < 0).any():
60:            masked_dims.add(dim)
61:        elif np.array_equal(indxr, np.arange(dim_sizes.get(dim, 0))):
62:            unchanged_dims.add(dim)
63:
64:    for name, var in variables.items():
65:        if isinstance(fill_value, dict):
66:            fill_value_ = fill_value.get(name, dtypes.NA)
67:        else:
68:            fill_value_ = fill_value
69:
70:        if sparse:
71:            var = var._as_sparse(fill_value=fill_value_)
72:        indxr = tuple(
73:            slice(None) if d in unchanged_dims else dim_pos_indexers.get(d, slice(None))
74:            for d in var.dims
75:        )
76:        needs_masking = any(d in masked_dims for d in var.dims)
77:
78:        if needs_masking:
79:            new_var = var._getitem_with_mask(indxr, fill_value=fill_value_)
80:        elif all(is_full_slice(k) for k in indxr):
81:            # no reindexing necessary
82:            # here we need to manually deal with copying data, since
83:            # we neither created a new ndarray nor used fancy indexing
84:            new_var = var.copy(deep=copy)
85:        else:
86:            new_var = var[indxr]
87:
88:        new_variables[name] = new_var
89:
90:    return new_variables

103:    For internal use only, not public API.

106:    aligner = Aligner(*objects, **kwargs)
107:    aligner.align()
108:    aligned_objects = aligner.results
109:
110:    """

113:    results: tuple[T_Alignable, ...]

143:        sparse: bool = False,

276:    def find_matching_unindexed_dims(self) -> None:
277:        unindexed_dim_sizes = defaultdict(set)
278:
279:        for obj in self.objects:
280:            for dim in obj.dims:

282:                    unindexed_dim_sizes[dim].add(obj.sizes[dim])

286:    def assert_no_index_conflict(self) -> None:
287:        """Check for uniqueness of both coordinate and dimension names across all sets
288:        of matching indexes.
289:
290:        We need to make sure that all indexes used for re-indexing or alignment
291:        are fully compatible and do not conflict each other.
292:
293:        Note: perhaps we could choose less restrictive constraints and instead
294:        check for conflicts among the dimension (position) indexers returned by
295:        `Index.reindex_like()` for each matching pair of object index / aligned
296:        index?
297:        (ref: https://github.com/pydata/xarray/issues/1603#issuecomment-442965602)
298:
299:        """
300:        matching_keys = set(self.all_indexes) | set(self.indexes)
301:
302:        coord_count: dict[Hashable, int] = defaultdict(int)
303:        dim_count: dict[Hashable, int] = defaultdict(int)
304:        for coord_names_dims, _ in matching_keys:
305:            dims_set: set[Hashable] = set()
306:            for name, dims in coord_names_dims:
307:                coord_count[name] += 1
308:                dims_set.update(dims)
309:            for dim in dims_set:
310:                dim_count[dim] += 1
311:
312:        for count, msg in [(coord_count, "coordinates"), (dim_count, "dimensions")]:
313:            dup = {k: v for k, v in count.items() if v > 1}
314:            if dup:
315:                items_msg = ", ".join(
316:                    f"{k!r} ({v} conflicting indexes)" for k, v in dup.items()
317:                )
318:                raise ValueError(
319:                    "cannot re-index or align objects with conflicting indexes found for "
320:                    f"the following {msg}: {items_msg}\n"
321:                    "Conflicting indexes may occur when\n"
322:                    "- they relate to different sets of coordinate and/or dimension names\n"
323:                    "- they don't have the same type\n"
324:                    "- they may be used to reindex data along common dimensions"
325:                )
326:
327:    def _need_reindex(self, dim, cmp_indexes) -> bool:
328:        """Whether or not we need to reindex variables for a set of
329:        matching indexes.
330:
331:        We don't reindex when all matching indexes are equal for two reasons:
332:        - It's faster for the usual case (already aligned objects).
333:        - It ensures it's possible to do operations that don't require alignment
334:          on indexes with duplicate values (which cannot be reindexed with
335:          pandas). This is useful, e.g., for overwriting such duplicate indexes.
336:
337:        """
338:        if not indexes_all_equal(cmp_indexes):
339:            # always reindex when matching indexes are not equal
340:            return True
341:
342:        unindexed_dims_sizes = {}
343:        for d in dim:
344:            if d in self.unindexed_dim_sizes:
345:                sizes = self.unindexed_dim_sizes[d]
346:                if len(sizes) > 1:
347:                    # reindex if different sizes are found for unindexed dims
348:                    return True
349:                else:
350:                    unindexed_dims_sizes[d] = next(iter(sizes))
351:
352:        if unindexed_dims_sizes:
353:            indexed_dims_sizes = {}
354:            for cmp in cmp_indexes:
355:                index_vars = cmp[1]
356:                for var in index_vars.values():
357:                    indexed_dims_sizes.update(var.sizes)
358:
359:            for d, size in unindexed_dims_sizes.items():
360:                if indexed_dims_sizes.get(d, -1) != size:
361:                    # reindex if unindexed dimension size doesn't match
362:                    return True
363:
364:        return False
365:
366:    def _get_index_joiner(self, index_cls) -> Callable:
367:        if self.join in ["outer", "inner"]:
368:            return functools.partial(
369:                functools.reduce,
370:                functools.partial(index_cls.join, how=self.join),
371:            )
372:        elif self.join == "left":
373:            return operator.itemgetter(0)
374:        elif self.join == "right":
375:            return operator.itemgetter(-1)
376:        elif self.join == "override":
377:            # We rewrite all indexes and then use join='left'
378:            return operator.itemgetter(0)
379:        else:
380:            # join='exact' return dummy lambda (error is raised)
381:            return lambda _: None
382:
383:    def align_indexes(self) -> None:
384:        """Compute all aligned indexes and their corresponding coordinate variables."""
385:
386:        aligned_indexes = {}
387:        aligned_index_vars = {}
388:        reindex = {}
389:        new_indexes = {}
390:        new_index_vars = {}
391:
392:        for key, matching_indexes in self.all_indexes.items():
393:            matching_index_vars = self.all_index_vars[key]
394:            dims = {d for coord in matching_index_vars[0].values() for d in coord.dims}
395:            index_cls = key[1]
396:
397:            if self.join == "override":
398:                joined_index = matching_indexes[0]
399:                joined_index_vars = matching_index_vars[0]
400:                need_reindex = False
401:            elif key in self.indexes:
402:                joined_index = self.indexes[key]
403:                joined_index_vars = self.index_vars[key]
404:                cmp_indexes = list(
405:                    zip(
406:                        [joined_index] + matching_indexes,
407:                        [joined_index_vars] + matching_index_vars,
408:                        strict=True,
409:                    )
410:                )
411:                need_reindex = self._need_reindex(dims, cmp_indexes)
412:            else:
413:                if len(matching_indexes) > 1:
414:                    need_reindex = self._need_reindex(
415:                        dims,
416:                        list(zip(matching_indexes, matching_index_vars, strict=True)),
417:                    )
418:                else:
419:                    need_reindex = False
420:                if need_reindex:
421:                    if self.join == "exact":
422:                        raise ValueError(
423:                            "cannot align objects with join='exact' where "
424:                            "index/labels/sizes are not equal along "
425:                            "these coordinates (dimensions): "
426:                            + ", ".join(f"{name!r} {dims!r}" for name, dims in key[0])
427:                        )
428:                    joiner = self._get_index_joiner(index_cls)
429:                    joined_index = joiner(matching_indexes)
430:                    if self.join == "left":
431:                        joined_index_vars = matching_index_vars[0]
432:                    elif self.join == "right":
433:                        joined_index_vars = matching_index_vars[-1]
434:                    else:
435:                        joined_index_vars = joined_index.create_variables()
436:                else:
437:                    joined_index = matching_indexes[0]
438:                    joined_index_vars = matching_index_vars[0]
439:
440:            reindex[key] = need_reindex
441:            aligned_indexes[key] = joined_index
442:            aligned_index_vars[key] = joined_index_vars
443:
444:            for name, var in joined_index_vars.items():
445:                new_indexes[name] = joined_index
446:                new_index_vars[name] = var
447:
448:        # Explicitly provided indexes that are not found in objects to align
449:        # may relate to unindexed dimensions so we add them too
450:        for key, idx in self.indexes.items():
451:            if key not in aligned_indexes:
452:                index_vars = self.index_vars[key]
453:                reindex[key] = False
454:                aligned_indexes[key] = idx
455:                aligned_index_vars[key] = index_vars
456:                for name, var in index_vars.items():
457:                    new_indexes[name] = idx
458:                    new_index_vars[name] = var

460:        self.aligned_indexes = aligned_indexes"}

680:    *objects: T_Alignable,
681:    join: JoinOptions = "inner",
682:    copy: bool = True,
683:    indexes=None,
684:    exclude: str | Iterable[Hashable] = frozenset(),
685:    fill_value=dtypes.NA,
686:) -> tuple[T_Alignable, ...]:
687:    """
688:    Given any number of Dataset and/or DataArray objects, returns new
689:    objects with aligned indexes and dimension sizes.
690:
691:    Array from the aligned objects are suitable as input to mathematical
692:    operators, because along each dimension they have the same index and size.
693:
694:    Missing values (if ``join != 'inner'``) are filled with ``fill_value``.
695:    The default fill value is NaN.
696:
697:    Parameters
698:    ----------
699:    *objects : Dataset or DataArray
700:        Objects to align.
701:    join : {"outer", "inner", "left", "right", "exact", "override"}, optional
702:        Method for joining the indexes of the passed objects along each
703:        dimension:
704:
705:        - "outer": use the union of object indexes
706:        - "inner": use the intersection of object indexes
707:        - "left": use indexes from the first object with each dimension
708:        - "right": use indexes from the last object with each dimension
709:        - "exact": instead of aligning, raise `ValueError` when indexes to be
710:          aligned are not equal
711:        - "override": if indexes are of same size, rewrite indexes to be
712:          those of the first object with that dimension. Indexes for the same
713:          dimension must have the same size in all objects.
714:
715:    copy : bool, default: True
716:        If ``copy=True``, data in the return values is always copied. If
717:        ``copy=False`` and reindexing is unnecessary, or can be performed with
718:        only slice operations, then the output may share memory with the input.
719:        In either case, new xarray objects are always returned.
720:    indexes : dict-like, optional
721:        Any indexes explicitly provided with the `indexes` argument should be
722:        used in preference to the aligned indexes.
723:    exclude : str, iterable of hashable or None, optional
724:        Dimensions that must be excluded from alignment
725:    fill_value : scalar or dict-like, optional
726:        Value to use for newly missing values. If a dict-like, maps
727:        variable names to fill values. Use a data array's name to
728:        refer to its values.
729:
730:    Returns
731:    -------
732:    aligned : tuple of DataArray or Dataset
733:        Tuple of objects with the same type as `*objects` with aligned
734:        coordinates.
735:
736:    Raises
737:    ------
738:    ValueError
739:        If any dimensions without labels on the arguments have different sizes,
740:        or a different size than the size of the aligned dimension labels.
741:
742:    Examples
743:    --------
744:    >>> x = xr.DataArray(
745:    ...     [[25, 35], [10, 24]],
746:    ...     dims=("lat", "lon"),
747:    ...     coords={"lat": [35.0, 40.0], "lon": [100.0, 120.0]},
748:    ... )
749:    >>> y = xr.DataArray(
750:    ...     [[20, 5], [7, 13]],
751:    ...     dims=("lat", "lon"),
752:    ...     coords={"lat": [35.0, 42.0], "lon": [100.0, 120.0]},
753:    ... )
754:
755:    >>> x
756:    <xarray.DataArray (lat: 2, lon: 2)> Size: 32B
757:    array([[25, 35],
758:           [10, 24]])
759:    Coordinates:
760:      * lat      (lat) float64 16B 35.0 40.0
761:      * lon      (lon) float64 16B 100.0 120.0
762:
763:    >>> y
764:    <xarray.DataArray (lat: 2, lon: 2)> Size: 32B
765:    array([[20,  5],
766:           [ 7, 13]])
767:    Coordinates:
768:      * lat      (lat) float64 16B 35.0 42.0
769:      * lon      (lon) float64 16B 100.0 120.0
770:
771:    >>> a, b = xr.align(x, y)
772:    >>> a
773:    <xarray.DataArray (lat: 1, lon: 2)> Size: 16B
774:    array([[25, 35]])
775:    Coordinates:
776:      * lat      (lat) float64 8B 35.0
777:      * lon      (lon) float64 16B 100.0 120.0
778:    >>> b
779:    <xarray.DataArray (lat: 1, lon: 2)> Size: 16B
780:    array([[20,  5]])
781:    Coordinates:
782:      * lat      (lat) float64 8B 35.0
783:      * lon      (lon) float64 16B 100.0 120.0
784:
785:    >>> a, b = xr.align(x, y, join="outer")
786:    >>> a
787:    <xarray.DataArray (lat: 3, lon: 2)> Size: 48B
788:    array([[25., 35.],
789:           [10., 24.],
790:           [nan, nan]])
791:    Coordinates:
792:      * lat      (lat) float64 24B 35.0 40.0 42.0
793:      * lon      (lon) float64 16B 100.0 120.0
794:    >>> b
795:    <xarray.DataArray (lat: 3, lon: 2)> Size: 48B
796:    array([[20.,  5.],
797:           [nan, nan],
798:           [ 7., 13.]])
799:    Coordinates:
800:      * lat      (lat) float64 24B 35.0 40.0 42.0
801:      * lon      (lon) float64 16B 100.0 120.0
802:
803:    >>> a, b = xr.align(x, y, join="outer", fill_value=-999)
804:    >>> a
805:    <xarray.DataArray (lat: 3, lon: 2)> Size: 48B
806:    array([[  25,   35],
807:           [  10,   24],
808:           [-999, -999]])

810:      * lat      (lat) float64 24B 35.0 40.0 42.0
